A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original 160M-parameter pretraining experiments, estimator ablations, held-out performance predictions and loss-matrix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds 410M-parameter experiments and DCLM evaluations extending to 1.4B parameters.

M1.justification: The rank-correlation estimator, capped linear projection and optional fastText classifier remain unchanged; Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A. Spearman estimation was already evaluated in v1, and page-level estimation was already specified in its preregistration. v2 adds validation, theoretical support and configuration details for these approaches.

E1.justification: v1 actually evaluates RPJv2 pretraining data and eight benchmarks, while DCLM experiments are only planned. v2 evaluates raw and extensively prefiltered DCLM pools and the 22-benchmark DCLM Core aggregate. It also evaluates an aggregate of the four retained non-English LAMBADA tasks; these are not newly added languages.

E2.justification: The original comparison retains uniform sampling, language filtering, DSIR and handcrafted fastText. The added scaling comparisons use narrower comparator sets: Figure 11 compares against uniform sampling alone, while Figure 3 includes uniform sampling and handcrafted fastText. No new external baseline family is introduced.

E3.justification: v2 adds 410M/8.2B-token experiments and DCLM experiments up to 1.4B/28.8B tokens. Appendix N replaces the preregistered DCLM training/evaluation pipeline with custom Pythia training and Eleuther Eval Harness, and uses a 10% random sample of the planned 1.64T-token pool. Appendix M repeats the selected 3.2B tokens while allowing the uniform baseline 8.2B unique tokens.

E4.justification: Figure 3 and Appendices M–N add substantial tests of scaling and external validity, including raw versus prefiltered pools, domain-level versus page-level estimation, and scaling with duplicated selected data. Appendix O adds task-specific lists of the most correlated domains. The earlier estimator/projection ablations, language analyses and PCA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The retained prediction analysis has the same 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, standard-deviation bands and p=0.035 comparison, with the R2 figure moved to Appendix I. v2 adds no reported seed counts, repeated-run procedures or uncertainty estimates for its scaling results.

E6.justification: The original tables and result plots retain their values. New Figure 3 reports, for example, approximately 0.21 versus 0.10 DCLM Core performance for domain-level correlations versus handcrafted fastText at 1.4B on the raw pool, but near parity on the prefiltered pool. Figure 11 adds 410M results showing wins over uniform sampling on seven of eight tasks. These are additional settings, not revised 160M scores.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds two lemmas and a derivation relating Spearman rank correlation to single-index-model coefficient ordering. Appendix B.1 also repairs v1 Appendix A.1's Gaussian-variance argument by explicitly expanding the variance of independent components. The original principal theorem statements and projection results are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: v1's validated empirical claims concern 160M models, with larger-scale generalization left to future tests. v2's abstract and introduction claim advantages that increase with scale up to 1.4B, and superiority over handcrafted fastText on raw DCLM data while remaining close on prefiltered data. This substantially broadens the claimed empirical scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a focused applicability boundary: extensive prior filtering leaves little benefit from correlation-based selection. Figure 3 attributes this to the narrowly distributed correlations in the prefiltered pool. Appendix N also explains why architecture and evaluation-code differences prevent direct comparison with published DCLM scores. Earlier interpretations of language selection and prediction outliers largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds access information for a documented pip package and repository. Appendix N substantially extends implementation documentation with DCLM estimator sample sizes, minimum pages per domain, the 50% token threshold used to construct classifier labels, filter reuse across scales, and custom training/evaluation choices. The original hardware and hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Huang et al. (2024) on compression and intelligence, Marion et al. (2023) on pretraining-data pruning, and Korotkov and Korotkov (2019) for an integral used in the new proof. The central positioning relative to observational scaling, proxy-model selection and handcrafted filters remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: pseudocode, alternative-method discussion, language-mixture analysis, prediction-score discussion and PCA analysis move into appendices. A new main-text section summarizes completed preregistered experiments, while their detailed account moves to Appendix N. The introduction and results narrative are revised around this structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel scaling plot in Figure 3 and the 410M heatmap in Figure 11. It resizes the main benchmark heatmap and relocates several existing figures, including language distributions, R2 scores and PCA plots, into the appendices. Original plotted data remain intact, but the visual organization changes substantially.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left scaling and external validity unresolved. v2 supplies substantial validation on new DCLM pools up to 1.4B parameters, reports the lack of gains after extensive filtering, and repairs an existing proof step. This materially strengthens the evidence and applicability guidance. Appendix N transparently discloses departures from the preregistration, although the custom evaluation prevents direct comparison with published DCLM scores and the new scaling results lack run-level uncertainty reporting.
